work.title: Define the skill manifest schema and skill identity
work.description: Give a skill a machine-readable identity the Core can validate: id, version, kind, declared capabilities, and a content digest, declared beside SKILL.md and parsed strictly. Follows the conventions src/core/initiative.ts already sets — an exported schema version and type, an id regex beside the others in src/core/identifiers.ts, a parser that refuses unknown fields, and a slugOf-style rule for anything derived from prose. Identity and validation only: no resolution, no dependency evaluation, no persistence on a run. Kinds start at the two the repository can justify today, stage and secondary; more are additive later. The seven shipped skills gain manifests, and package.json already ships skills/, so they travel with the release.
acceptance: A skill manifest parses only with a valid id, version, kind, and declared capabilities, and a misspelled or unknown field is refused rather than dropped
Every skill under skills/ carries a manifest that parses, and its content digest is reproducible from the skill file alone
A CLI read lists the available skills with their id, version, kind, and digest, and changes nothing
Skill files stay harness-neutral: no manifest names a harness, and src/test/harness-adapters.test.ts still passes

result.summary: Skill manifest schema decided: skills/<id>/skill.json parsed strictly by a new src/core/skill.ts (schemaVersion 1, type codepatrol-skill, id/version/kind/capabilities/digest), digest = sha256 of SKILL.md bytes, kinds stage|secondary, and a read-only `codepatrol skill list` that verifies every shipped manifest against its SKILL.md.
result.handoff:
# Plan: Define the skill manifest schema and skill identity (INIT-1.1)

## Product files Build touches
1. src/core/identifiers.ts — add `SKILL_ID = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/` beside the existing regexes.
2. src/core/skill.ts (new) — schema constants, type, strict parser, serializer, digest helper.
3. src/cli/commands/skill.ts (new) — `skill list` command plus an exported `listShippedSkills(directory)` helper.
4. src/cli/command.ts — add "skill" to the CommandSpec name union.
5. src/cli/registry.ts — register skillCommand with the other reads (after initiativeCommand).
6. skills/<name>/skill.json — one manifest per shipped skill (7 files).
7. src/test/skill.test.ts (new).

No other files change. In particular harness-adapters.test.ts, opencode.json, and the .claude/.opencode adapters are untouched.

## Schema (src/core/skill.ts)
```ts
export const SKILL_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1;
export const SKILL_TYPE = "codepatrol-skill";
export const SKILL_KINDS = ["stage", "secondary"] as const;
export type SkillKind = (typeof SKILL_KINDS)[number];
export interface SkillManifest {
  schemaVersion: typeof SKILL_SCHEMA_VERSION;
  type: typeof SKILL_TYPE;
  id: string;
  version: string;
  kind: SkillKind;
  capabilities: string[];
  digest: string;
}
```
- parseSkillManifest mirrors parseInitiative exactly: same object/keys/text/corrupt helper pattern, unknown or missing fields refuse with STATE_CORRUPT (acceptance 1).
- Field rules: schemaVersion === 1; type === "codepatrol-skill"; id matches SKILL_ID from identifiers.ts; version matches /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/; kind in SKILL_KINDS; capabilities is an array of unique tokens each matching /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/ (empty array allowed); digest matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.
- serializeSkillManifest writes the fixed key order above plus a trailing newline, like serializeInitiative.
- skillContentDigest(contents: string | Buffer) returns sha256(contents) from src/core/json.ts.
- The module is pure: no filesystem, no node:fs imports (the layering rule version.ts states — core and application stay filesystem-free).

## Placement and identity rules
- Manifest file: skills/<id>/skill.json beside SKILL.md. Naming mirrors work.json/initiative.json (the file is named after its document type). The .claude/skills entries symlink whole directories and opencode.json points at ./skills, so the sibling travels everywhere SKILL.md does; every harness reads only SKILL.md, so the JSON is inert (acceptance 4). package.json already lists "skills" in files.
- manifest.id must equal its directory name. The parser cannot check this (filesystem-free); the CLI read and the tests enforce it.
- digest is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes of SKILL.md alone. The manifest never participates in its own digest (acceptance 2).
- Kinds: codepatrol-plan, codepatrol-review, codepatrol-build, codepatrol-verify, codepatrol-ship are "stage" (matching STAGES in src/core/types.ts:1); codepatrol-spec and codepatrol-work are "secondary".
- version starts at "1.0.0" for all seven.
- capabilities: all seven declare ["cli"] — the one requirement every shipped skill genuinely has (each drives the codepatrol CLI). The vocabulary is deliberately open; tokens are additive later, exactly as kinds are.

## CLI read: codepatrol skill list
- New CommandSpec in src/cli/commands/skill.ts following commands/initiative.ts: name "skill", usage ["skill list"], no flags, exactPositionals 0.
- The skills directory resolves package-relative — path.resolve(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), "../../../skills") — the same pattern as version.ts, because the read reports what this codepatrol installation ships, not workspace state. It never touches --workspace, needs no remote, and writes nothing (acceptance 3).
- listShippedSkills(directory): for each entry directory, read skill.json, parseSkillManifest (a corrupt manifest fails the command), require id === directory name, recompute the digest from SKILL.md and require equality with the recorded digest — a mismatch throws STATE_CORRUPT, because an identity that does not reproduce is corruption, not a soft warning.
- Output, sorted by id:
```json
{ "skills": [ { "id": "...", "version": "...", "kind": "...", "capabilities": ["cli"], "digest": "..." } ] }
```
- Registered in registry.ts COMMANDS so --help lists it.

## Tests (src/test/skill.test.ts)
- Parser: valid manifest round-trips through serialize/parse; an unknown field is refused; a misspelled field (e.g. "capability") is refused as a missing required field; bad id, bad version, bad kind, and bad digest are each refused; duplicate capabilities refused; empty capabilities accepted.
- Shipped skills: every skills/*/skill.json parses; id equals the directory name; the digest recomputed from SKILL.md equals the recorded digest (reproducibility); kinds match the STAGES split; no manifest mentions a harness name (guard mirroring harness-adapters.test.ts).
- CLI: listShippedSkills returns the seven skills sorted by id; two consecutive calls return identical output (changes nothing).
- Existing suites must pass unchanged: npm run typecheck, npm test (including harness-adapters.test.ts), npm run smoke — i.e. npm run verify.

## Acceptance coverage
1. Strict parse with refused unknown/misspelled fields — parser + parser tests.
2. Every skill under skills/ carries a parsing manifest; digest reproducible from SKILL.md alone — 7 manifests + shipped-skills test.
3. CLI read lists id/version/kind/digest and changes nothing — skill list + CLI test.
4. Harness neutrality — manifests contain no harness names; guard test; harness-adapters.test.ts passes untouched.

## Non-goals (per the Work text)
No resolution, no dependency evaluation, no persistence on a run (INIT-1.2, INIT-1.4). No capability vocabulary beyond "cli". schemaVersion stays 1.

traces.message: Conventions confirmed: exported schema version + type + strict unknown-field-refusing parser in src/core/initiative.ts, id regexes in src/core/identifiers.ts, sha256 in src/core/json.ts, read-only CommandSpec pattern in src/cli/commands/initiative.ts, package-relative resource reads in src/cli/version.ts with the rule that core and application stay filesystem-free.

Skill manifest lives at skills/<id>/skill.json beside SKILL.md: naming mirrors work.json/initiative.json, whole-directory symlinks and opencode skills.paths carry the sibling, harnesses read only SKILL.md so the manifest is inert to them, and package.json already ships skills/.

Digest is the hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes of SKILL.md alone, via sha256 from src/core/json.ts; the manifest never participates in its own digest. Kinds: the five STAGES skills are stage, codepatrol-spec and codepatrol-work are secondary. Every shipped manifest declares capabilities ["cli"], the single honest shared requirement; the vocabulary is additive.

CLI read is codepatrol skill list: no flags, resolves the shipped skills directory package-relative like version.ts, parses each skill.json strictly, requires id == directory name and recorded digest == recomputed digest (mismatch fails with STATE_CORRUPT), outputs id/version/kind/capabilities/digest sorted by id, and writes nothing.
